Huge thank you to Jireh and Anne who reviewed #37779 and got it in. Now the annoying task is to use the classes various (function) spaces. By the nature of refactors, these will pick up merge conflicts very easily, so I would be happy if these get reviewed reasonably quickly.
A complete list of what is to be done is in #39639
#39657 abstract version of sum_apply (not super urgent, but would make all of the refactors a bit easier)
#39637 use IsApply for ContinuousLinearMap
I would like to ping the two PRs above
#40450 vector measures (there is some nontrivial changes here)
#40466 multilinear maps
#40463 continuous multilinear maps
#40607 ContDiffMapSupportedIn
#40608 TestFunction
#39638 LinearMap (I ran into some issues with some homology stuff, where the proofs became way more involved and I can't see why, but I suspect something is wrong somewhere else)
I have just left a review on 39638: much of it is just great and a clear improvement. Help with understanding the proofs that get worse is welcome, I have noted them in the review!
Thanks! Quick answer about the dsimp: it is expected that dsimp has to be replaced by simp because class lemmas can never be defeq lemmas as there is no way of saying 'all proofs have to be by rfl'
Of course, thanks for explaining!

I had a look into the simpNF issue in #39638: I am very much confused why this is not a problem on master. The lhs of one of the auto-generated lemmas gets simplified by the lemma that gets flagged in the PR, so if I understand the simpNF linter correctly, then that should be not ok.
#40945: outer measures
#40840: measures
#40899: abbrevs for pointwise multiplication (is needed in a few other PRs)
the two measure PRs would be great to get in, so that I can test a typeclass for coercions between FunLike types - that should be able to get rid of some other boilerplate

Moritz Doll said:

so that I can test a typeclass for coercions between FunLike types

@Moritz Doll The only thing I can imagine this means scares me. Can you extrapolate on this coercion in this thread please?
it is #40277. I agree it is slightly scary, but I don't think it is totally insane. However, I do want a real world test and see whether it has a horrible impact on typeclass synthesis

It doesn't look terribly useful to me, but maybe I'm missing the point. However, it's not what I thought it was, so I'm no longer scared. I thought you were defining some new thing and making it a coercion; instead, you are simply taking a coercion as an argument.

If you look for instance at the basic file for CLMs, you will find a lot of lemmas of the form docs#ContinuousLinearMap.toLinearMap_add and docs#ContinuousLinearMap.toContinuousAddMonoidHom_add
these are all special cases of the lemmas in the PR above. Similar things exist for measure to outer measure, continuous multilinear map to multilinear map, etc.. getting rid of this is not super important, but it will only get harder the more mathlib grows

The problem is that your Coe lemmas won't actually apply to any coercion because you will basically never see docs#Coe.coe but a specific function like docs#ContinuousLinearMap.toLinearMap; you could maybe use your Coe lemmas to prove lemmas like ContinuousLinearMap.toLinearMap_add but that doesn't seem very useful because these lemmas are basically always rfl and a proof like coe_add_eq_add (M₁ →SL[σ₁₂] M₂) (F₂ := M₁ →ₛₗ[σ₁₂] M₂) f g would just be longer.
What's the point of these IsApply typeclasses? They look like the kind of typeclasses we've been working to remove...
what kind of typeclasses have we been trying to remove?
@Anne Baanen wrote very similar typeclasses just before the port to Lean 4, and we reverted them soon after

Yaël, I think you're generalizing a bit too much. The problem here is the IsCoeApply class specifically, since it contains a Coe. What I tried before we reverted it for Lean 4 is classes for coe (a * b) = coe a * coe b, which won't work for the same reason that Robin describes. IsMulApply etc are guaranteed to be indexed on DFunLike.coe, so they do work.

Yet I don't quite get the point of all these instances. To save us some boilerplate? Shouldn't we find a way to autogenerate the relevant lemmas once for each type of morphisms, rather than paying the cost of TC search every single time one of these lemmas gets used(/tried)?
@Yaël Dillies Would you want to auto-generate docs#tsum_apply for every applicable morphism?
I have never written tsum_apply for any of my morphism types. Is it really widely used?
I think that's kind of the point, we now get it automatically for every summation and every morphism
I recently needed it for Bessel functions (#42825). It comes from the fderiv of FormalMultilinearSeries

https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/287929-mathlib4/topic/AddMonoidHomClass.20confusion/with/502885117
Also we get rid of various (very boring) definitions for the coercion bundled as a linear map/additive group homomorphism/whatever. And it cleans up a lot of very inefficient code, where people used overly elaborate proofs for trivial results.
And we don't even have a typeclass for composition, which get rid of fair number of other trivial lemmas, or a typeclass for .symm for Equiv, which together with composition would get rid of a lot of boilerplate lemmas.
